sections.label: NLB Act electronic deposit amendments
sections.summary: The amendments require publishers to deposit one electronic copy within four weeks and let NLB copy online material on Singapore websites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the NLB Act are a step forward to preserve and eternalise Singapore’s digital heritage, by collecting electronic publications through legal deposits, and by preserving Singapore domain websites through web archiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Part of the amendment mandates publishers to deposit one copy of any electronic publication within four weeks of publication, on top of existing requirements to deposit two physical copies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, under section 7(2)(f) of the Bill, it is stated that NLB is allowed "to make copies of any online material made available on a Singapore website, at the times and in the manner the Board considers appropriate." Unlike physical copies where there is a limited number of books deposited in libraries, such an amendment will technically allow the Board to make unlimited digital copies of the publisher's work.

sections.label: Archived items mostly physical
sections.summary: Close to 1.3 million items have been archived, and a vast majority are physical hardcopy publications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Up to date, close to 1.3 million items have been archived and a vast majority, if not all of these items, are in the form of physical "hardcopy" publications, such as books, magazines or written papers.

sections.label: Voluntary deposit and NLB archiving
sections.summary: Publishers and authors can voluntarily deposit electronic copies, and the speaker agrees with changes empowering NLB to archive online materials more expeditiously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, publishers and authors can voluntarily deposit electronic copies of their publications with NLB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Both methods can be cumbersome and laborious, often yielding results that are not proportionate to the effort that is put in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I agree with the proposed changes to the Act that will empower NLB to archive online materials more expeditiously and facilitate the records keeping process.

sections.label: Expanding library materials definition
sections.summary: The speaker says annual snapshots may not suffice and calls expanding library materials to include electronic and online material important and sensible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Second, taking an annual snapshot might not be enough, given the speed at which content is created and then replaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, the move to expand the definition of "library materials" to include electronic materials and any online material made available on a Singapore website is an important one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Similarly, the move from a scheme based on voluntary deposit of content to one where NLB has the right to make copies of library materials is a sensible reflection of the current media environment.

sections.label: Access restricted to two terminals
sections.summary: The current proposal is to restrict access to two terminals at NLB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The current proposal is to restrict access to two terminals at NLB.

sections.label: Preserving Singapore-related online content
sections.summary: The amendment aims to collect and preserve Singapore-related online content for future generations, starting with all .sg domain websites.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The intent of this amendment is to ensure that Singapore-related content, which is increasingly found online, is collected and preserved for future generations so that they can better understand the evolution of events here.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, in the first instance, NLB will collect material from all .sg domain websites.

sections.label: Blocking objectionable archived content
sections.summary: NLB may block access to archived websites containing content objectionable under relevant laws or codes.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If the websites archived are found to contain content that is found to be objectionable under the relevant laws or codes, then NLB may block access to that content.

sections.label: Public access at Lee Kong Chian
sections.summary: NLB will initially provide public access to collected electronic publications and websites at the Lee Kong Chian Reference Library.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To strike a balance as we embark on this new scheme, NLB will, for a start, provide public access to the collected electronic publications and websites at the Lee Kong Chian Reference Library located at the National Library Building.

sections.label: Digital content copyright stays with creators
sections.summary: Under the proposed amendments, copyright of digital content continues to reside with content creators and publishers.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In time to come, we hope to be able to share a greater collection of materials on NLB's digital platforms through the support of content creators and publishers as they join us in our efforts to make our nation's published heritage accessible in more ways.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I want to assure all Members that under the proposed amendments, the copyright of digital content continues to reside with the content creators and publishers.

sections.label: Processing time before public access
sections.summary: Processing including quality check and cataloguing may take one to six months before material is accessible to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As there are several steps involved in the processing of material, which includes quality check and cataloguing, it may take one to six months from the date of collection – depending on the type of material collected – before it is made accessible to the public.

sections.label: Preserving materials through format migration
sections.summary: Migration to updated formats prevents corruption or loss, and the amendments let NLB preserve materials for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This includes the migration of content to updated formats from time to time, which will prevent content from being corrupted or lost when formats become obsolete.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I want to reiterate that the proposed amendments to the Act will be an important step forward in allowing NLB to preserve the materials which document Singapore's history and culture, so that these can be made available to our future generations.
